title: Amit Shah launches 'SHE Mart' in Kerala, says cooperatives key to women's empowerment - Moneycontrol.com
full_text:
Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah on Saturday inaugurated a series of initiatives of the National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India Limited (NCCF) in Kollam’s Kundara, aimed at strengthening the cooperative sector and promoting women’s empowerment.
Addressing the event, Shah said the demand for a separate Cooperation Ministry at the Centre had existed since Independence but was fulfilled only after the Narendra Modi government created the ministry.
“PM Narendra Modi created the Cooperation Ministry and took a major step towards rural development, agricultural development and women's empowerment in the country,” he said.
Shah said Kerala had a long-standing cooperative tradition, with organised cooperative activity existing in regions such as Travancore, Cochin and Malabar even before Independence. He said more than 23,000 cooperatives were currently functioning in the state.
“Keralam is a very old state with strong cooperative infrastructure. More than 23,000 cooperatives are running very well here,” Shah said, while inviting Kerala’s Cooperation Minister to Delhi to explore the Centre’s schemes.
He said the Centre could provide special assistance and guidance to Kerala in areas including dairy, seeds and organic agriculture.
The minister launched the ‘SHE Mart’ initiative in Kerala under the SHE Mart Mission announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in the 2026-27 Union Budget. The initiative seeks to connect women self-help groups (SHGs) and rural industry entrepreneurs directly with markets and consumers.
“The concept of this 'SHE Mart' is a kind of self-help entrepreneur mart and is a very good effort to connect women SHG and rural industry entrepreneurs directly with the market and directly with the consumers,” Shah said.
He said Indian-brand and local products would be made available through more than 2,500 NCCF retail outlets, along with more than 300 SHE Mart stores across Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
As part of the initiatives, NCCF and NAFED mobile vans also began distributing onions, Bharat Atta and Bharat Rice to consumers in Kerala at affordable rates. Scholarships were also given to daughters of two farming families under the NAFED Welfare Scholarship Scheme.
Shah cited several measures taken under the Modi government while speaking about women’s empowerment. He said the share of women in the labour force had risen from 23 per cent in 2014-15 to 40 per cent, attributing the increase to facilities provided to women workers.
He said bank accounts had been opened for nearly 36 crore women and noted that paid maternity leave had been increased to 26 weeks.
“Today, over 11,000 daughters are serving as officers in the Indian Armed Forces,” Shah said.
He also said the government had banned triple talaq to protect the rights of Muslim women and that Muslim women could now undertake Hajj without a male companion.
Shah further said the target of creating three crore Lakhpati Didis had been achieved before 2024, while the BJP-led government had set a target of increasing the number to six crore by 2029. A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG member whose annual household income exceeds Rs 1 lakh.
The minister said women’s empowerment through cooperatives remained a core objective of the government.
(With inputs from agencies)
